title: cicd.yaml
description: Developer-facing pipeline configuration. This is the only file app teams edit to control their CI/CD pipelines - it never contains Tekton, YAML pipeline steps, or infrastructure details. Validated fail-fast by the validate-cicd-config Task before any other pipeline step runs.

agent.description: Named build agent image from the platform catalog. Not a raw image reference - keeps step code portable and centrally patchable. Still required even when `script` is omitted, since unit tests always run inside this image regardless of build strategy.

script.description: Build script the platform runs inside the agent image before packaging. Must be bash. Omit entirely for teams doing the whole build inside a multi-stage Containerfile - the separate build-source stage is skipped and kaniko builds `containerfile` directly. No default: presence/absence is the switch, so it can't silently mean 'skip' via an unrelated typo.

containerfile.description: Path to a multi-stage Containerfile kaniko builds directly - only consulted when build.script is omitted. "Containerfile" (not "Dockerfile") is this platform's deliberate, vendor-neutral term for the same OCI-buildable file format - kaniko itself has no opinion on the name, and it's the same file whichever name your repo uses.

platforms.description: Which architectures build-image.yaml builds and publishes as a real multi-arch image (via kaniko x N + a crane manifest-index combine - kaniko itself has no multi-arch capability). Defaults to both, since kiac-dev (arm64) and kind-prod (amd64) both run real workloads. Set to a single value only for an app that provably never deploys to the other cluster (e.g. backstage, a kind-prod-only singleton) - every kaniko run for an unrequested platform is skipped, not just unpublished, so this is a real build-time cost saving, not just a registry-tidiness knob.

artifacts.description: Additional non-container artifacts to build and publish alongside the primary container image, as real pullable OCI artifacts (oras push, not a container image) to <image-repo>:<version>-<type> - same registry and registry-credentials the image itself uses, no separate publish target. Independent of build.platforms/the image build: a service can publish both a container image AND a client-library wheel from the same source checkout. Empty by default - existing apps are unaffected. See build-artifact.yaml and docs/user/cicd-yaml-reference.md.

enabled.description: Persistent dependency-download cache for build-source (npm's package cache / Maven's local repository, not node_modules/target itself - see docs/cicd-yaml-reference.md). No `type` field: derived from `agent`'s prefix (nodejs-* -> npm, openjdk-* -> maven), not a second, redundantly-declarable field. Keyed by a hash of the relevant lockfile (package-lock.json/pom.xml) so a dependency change invalidates the cache automatically. A no-op (logged, not an error) for agents without cache support yet (python-*/go-1.22). Teams with no build.script (whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile) get layer caching for free from kaniko instead.

size.description: T-shirt size for this app's own cache PVC (small=1Gi, medium=2.5Gi, large=5Gi, xlarge=8Gi - same dictionary as the old cd-pipelines-user Helm chart's buildSpec.cacheSize). One PVC per app, specifically so this can vary per app. Chosen at onboarding time, not resizable live afterward - kind-observe's default storage class has allowVolumeExpansion: false, so changing this later means recreating the PVC (and losing its cached content), not a live resize.

T-shirt size for the ephemeral `source` workspace every stage's PipelineRun gets (small=2Gi, medium=5Gi, large=10Gi, xlarge=20Gi). This is the checked-out git repo plus build.script's own output plus kaniko's build context - distinct from build.cache (a separate, persistent, per-app dependency-download cache). Exists because a large build can genuinely fill this workspace's disk ('no space left on device'), not because of anything cache-related. Not per-stage: one size applies to every stage's source workspace for this app (build/test/deploy/release all declare the same `source` workspace shape), since build is normally the only stage large enough to need this, and a single per-app knob is simpler than one per stage. Not resizable live - each PipelineRun's workspace is a fresh, ephemeral volumeClaimTemplate-backed PVC (unlike build.cache's persistent one), so a size change just takes effect on the next run, nothing to migrate.

name.description: Name of the TestWorkflow to run (platform/<name>.yaml in this repo).

environments.description: The app's environments, defined once, in promotion order (the order of this list is the order a release walks). Unset: one Ground environment, dev. (It replaced lowerEnvironments, upperEnvironments and promotionOrder, removed 2026-10-07.) Each entry is a Ground environment (deployed automatically on push) or a Flight environment (deployed only through an approved release). Names must be unique. See docs/admin/adr/0019-environments-as-one-config-model.md.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter, at most 31 characters. Also used in the environment's namespace name.

tier.description: ground: deploys on every push. flight: deploys only through a release PR and its guardrails. For a cloud target (aws-ecs, aws-lambda, azure-container-apps) a flight environment is approved by a release pin PR on the source repo (glidepath/releases/<env>.yaml, ADR-0020) and sets no cluster.

cluster.description: Flight only, and only when the environment runs on a different cluster than the app's own (a cluster name from the platform cluster registry). A Ground environment cannot set it yet: Ground environments on other clusters are a future feature (docs/admin/known-gaps.md).

production.description: Marks the environment that serves real users and real data (ADR-0024). Must be a Flight environment, and for a Kubernetes target its cluster must be an upper cluster in the platform cluster registry (one nothing below it can write to, changed only through reviewed merges).

ecs.description: Cloud targets only. Overrides fields of deploy.ecs for this environment (for example service, or cluster); fields it does not set come from deploy.ecs. Only valid when deploy.target is aws-ecs.

lambda.description: Cloud targets only. Overrides fields of deploy.lambda for this environment (for example functionName); fields it does not set come from deploy.lambda. Only valid when deploy.target is aws-lambda.

azureContainerApps.description: Cloud targets only. Overrides fields of deploy.azureContainerApps for this environment (for example appName); fields it does not set come from deploy.azureContainerApps. Only valid when deploy.target is azure-container-apps.

chart.description: Kubernetes apps only. Overrides fields of deploy.chart (and through it the cluster default) for this environment, for example a newer targetRevision as a canary. Fields it does not set come from deploy.chart, then the cluster default.

strategy.description: deployment = native k8s Deployment rollout; rollout = Argo Rollouts (canary/blue-green). Rollout support has since landed and is the only strategy actually implemented (deploy-manifests.yaml manages an Argo Rollout unconditionally via the airframe-application chart - confirmed live, 2026-09-17): `deployment` is schema-valid but has NO effect - nothing renders a plain Deployment anymore. This is the reverse of this field's original meaning when it was first added (rollout was the future, unimplemented option then); kept as a two-value enum, default flipped, so an existing cicd.yaml that explicitly sets `strategy: deployment` still validates rather than breaking, even though it no longer describes real behavior.

releaseFile.description: Where the deploy/release stages write the machine-owned release record (release.image, releaseTracking) - see hangar/docs/autopilot/release-file-split.md (D9/AF-5). Exactly one `{env}` placeholder, substituted with the target environment name, matching deploy-manifests.yaml's own `${ENV}` variable. Schema-only today: no Task reads this field yet - deploy-manifests.yaml and open-release-pr.yaml still hardcode `platform/envs/${ENV}.yaml`/the gitops repo's `values.yaml`. The field exists now so the Airframe onboarding scaffold can start setting it (`airframe/envs/{env}.release.yaml`, once that directory exists) without a second wave of per-app cicd.yaml edits later. Default names a new, not-yet-existing Glidepath-owned path (`glidepath/`, distinct from Airframe's `platform/`/`airframe/` directory) for an app onboarded without an Airframe chart to layer a release file over - per the design doc's own default-path decision, not an existing convention anywhere else in this repo.

target.description: Where deploy.yaml's `deploy` stage actually deploys to. k8s-rollout (default) is the only target every existing app uses - deploy-manifests.yaml, Argo Rollouts via airframe-application, zero behavior change for an app that doesn't set this. The three cloud targets (added 2026-10-03/04) each require a matching config block below plus this app's own `secrets:` entries for cloud credentials (see docs/admin/app-secrets.md) - none are live-verified against a real account, see docs/admin/known-gaps.md. All three resolve correctly even for a git-rooted deploy (no build/test in that run) - resolve-deploy-target.yaml clones cicd.yaml directly via the GitHub App token broker in that case, rather than trusting an unpopulated config-json. - aws-ecs (deploy-ecs.yaml): registers a new ECS task-definition revision and updates the named service. Requires `deploy.ecs` and secrets `aws-access-key-id`/`aws-secret-access-key`. - aws-lambda (deploy-lambda.yaml): updates an existing function's container image. Requires `deploy.lambda` and the same AWS secrets as aws-ecs. Hard AWS constraint: image-repo must resolve to an Amazon ECR URI - Lambda cannot pull from an external registry like ghcr.io. - azure-container-apps (deploy-azure-container-apps.yaml): updates an existing Container App's image to a new revision. Requires `deploy.azureContainerApps` and secrets `azure-client-id`/`azure-client-secret`/`azure-tenant-id`.

chart.description: The Helm chart this app's environments render (ADR-0023). Unset: the cluster's default chart (Airframe's airframe-application). Fields not set here come from the cluster default, so pinning the default chart to another version is just targetRevision. A chart from another source sets repoURL, targetRevision, and path (git) or chart (a Helm or OCI registry); nothing is inherited from the default then. Only deploy.target k8s-rollout has a chart. A chart other than Airframe's must meet docs/admin/chart-contract.md.

repoURL.description: A git repository, or a Helm or OCI chart registry.

path.description: The chart directory inside a git repoURL, for example charts/my-chart.

chart.description: The chart name in a Helm or OCI registry repoURL.

targetRevision.description: A git tag, branch or commit; for a registry, the chart version. Pin a tag.

ecs.description: Required when deploy.target is aws-ecs; ignored otherwise.

service.description: ECS service name within that cluster.

containerName.description: Name of the container (within the task definition's containerDefinitions) whose image gets updated. Must match a real container name in the current task definition, or deploy-ecs.yaml fails loudly rather than silently updating nothing.

taskDefinitionFamily.description: Defaults to `<app-name>-<env>` if omitted - set this only when the real family name doesn't follow that convention.

lambda.description: Required when deploy.target is aws-lambda; ignored otherwise. The function must already exist (PackageType: Image) - deploy-lambda.yaml only updates its code, never creates it.

azureContainerApps.description: Required when deploy.target is azure-container-apps; ignored otherwise. The Container App must already exist (environment, ingress, scale rules, and any private-registry pull credentials already configured on it) - deploy-azure-container-apps.yaml only updates its image, never creates it.

appName.description: The Container App's own name, not this platform's app-name - name only when they differ.

ttl.description: How long an ephemeral environment lives after its last successful deploy before automatic teardown.

governance.description: Quality/security gates. sast/imageScan/policyCheck/sbom are real, live-enforcing gates (Semgrep/Trivy/gitsign+Fulcio/cosign SBOM attestation respectively - see docs/governance-stubs.md for exactly what each one verifies), not stubs.

policyCheck.description: Controls only the build-time shift-left copy of this scan, if one exists. The release-gate commit-signature check (catalog/tasks/verify-commit-signature.yaml) runs unconditionally on every release PR regardless of this flag - release gates are enforced, not app-configurable. Populate allowedCommitSigners below either way.

allowedCommitSigners.description: Plain email addresses gitsign's --certificate-identity-regexp is built from at verify time (see catalog/tasks/verify-commit-signature.yaml). Always consulted by the release-gate commit-signature check regardless of policyCheck's value - an app that leaves this empty fails that check on every release. One entry per allowed human signer; no regex syntax needed here.

scanResults.description: Shift-left notifications from sast-scan/image-scan the moment each real scan produces a result, separate from the general build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification above (which stays on whenever slack.enabled is true). Only takes effect when slack.enabled is also true. Defaults on (matching the pipeline's own default real-scan behavior), but an app that finds these too frequent/verbose can turn just this off without losing the general per-stage notifications.

enabled.description: Sends the same build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification as notifications.slack into Backstage's own Notifications plugin (broadcast to every Backstage user, viewable in Tower's Notifications tab), instead of/in addition to Slack. Independent toggle - either target can be on, off, or both. Requires the cluster's glidepath-catalog chart to have backstageBaseUrl and a glidepath-backstage-notify token secret configured (see docs/admin/notifications.md); a cluster without that setup skips silently.

secrets.description: Optional. Each entry pulls one key out of this Application's own backend secret store (assumed provisioned alongside the Application itself - see docs/app-secrets.md - NOT something platform-cicd creates) and lands it as a key in this Application's app-secrets Kubernetes Secret, synced by a real ExternalSecret. Open-ended by design: a brand-new secret purpose (SAST creds, a DB password, anything else a future Task needs) is a new list entry here, not a schema/template change - whatever Task consumes it just needs to know which `name` to look for. Empty by default: the SecretStore/ExternalSecret are only rendered at all when this list is non-empty, so an Application that doesn't use this feature gets no dangling resources pointed at a secrets namespace that may not exist for it.

name.description: Logical name. Becomes the key inside the app-secrets Kubernetes Secret this renders - a consuming Task mounts app-secrets and reads this exact filename. Also the default for `key` below, so the common case (the name you want to use here already matches the name it has in your backend store) needs only this one field.

key.description: Key name as it actually exists in the app's own backend secret store object. Defaults to `name` when omitted - only set this when the backend key is named differently than you want it exposed as.

pipelines.description: Optional named pipeline flows. Each flow can define a root trigger and an ordered list of stages, allowing app teams to describe build -> test -> deploy -> release sequences without writing Tekton YAML directly. The legacy list form used by earlier config files is also accepted and normalized by the chart.

source.description: Preferred explicit shape: git triggers evaluate branch/path filters; event triggers use the broker CDEvents path and the event field.

event.description: Explicit event identifier for the root trigger. For git sources this is the Git event kind; for event sources it is the CDEvents event type. No release.created - confirmed live that Pipelines-as-Code has no support for GitHub 'release' webhooks at all (any version): a real delivery came back '{"status":200,"message":"skipping non supported event"}', filtered out before PaC's own annotation matching ever runs, so no Trigger config could ever make this fire. Use 'tag' instead - publishing a GitHub Release also creates the underlying tag, which fires a real, working push event.

type.description: Legacy shorthand for the git-trigger form. Newer configs should use source+event.

tagPattern.description: Regex the pushed tag's name must match, required when event is 'tag' (e.g. 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'). See deliver-onboarding-files.yaml's generate_flow_file.

labels.description: Only meaningful when event is 'pull_request'. If set, the flow only fires for a PR carrying ALL of these GitHub labels (same all-must-match semantics as ArgoCD's own pullRequest generator labels: field, for consistency between the build trigger and the ephemeral-environment deploy trigger that reads the same PR). Omit for no label filter (fires on every PR touching this branch). See deliver-onboarding-files.yaml's generate_flow_file.

testName.description: Only meaningful on a test step. Overrides the top-level test.name for this specific step - needed when a flow has more than one test step (they'd otherwise be indistinguishable). Falls back to test.name when omitted; one of the two must resolve to a value, since a TestWorkflow run always needs a name. Not called `name` - that field below is the deploy/release target name, a different concept.

gitopsRepo.description: Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: the gitops repo (by name, e.g. 'gitops-cluster-kind-man') to open the image-bump PR against. Unlike release's gitops-<app-name> convention, this stage is for a hand-deployed singleton/cluster-config component whose manifests don't live in a per-app gitops repo, so the target repo must be named explicitly. Requires an extra Repository CR granting this app's CI namespace write access - see platformIdentity.extraGitopsRepos in the tenant identity.yaml (not this repo's cicd.yaml, since it's a trust/authorization grant the app owner doesn't self-serve).

manifestPath.description: Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: path within gitopsRepo to a plain Kubernetes manifest (not airframe-application Helm values.yaml) whose first container's image field gets patched, e.g. '60-backstage/backstage/deployment.yaml'.
